lines.en: Leo, if it rains on Saturday, we’ll visit the museum. Is that okay?
lines.pt: Leo, se chover no sábado, vamos visitar o museu. Está bem?

lines.en: Sure. If we go early, we’ll avoid the queue. Museums are busy at ten.
lines.pt: Claro. Se formos cedo, evitaremos a fila. Museus ficam cheios às dez.

lines.en: Good idea. If we buy tickets online, we’ll save some time too.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Se comprarmos ingressos pela internet, também vamos economizar tempo.

lines.en: And if the exhibition is boring, we’ll go to the gallery next door.
lines.pt: E se a exposição for chata, iremos à galeria ao lado.

lines.en: Fine. If you take an umbrella, I’ll bring a guide book for the city.
lines.pt: Certo. Se você levar um guarda-chuva, eu trago um guia da cidade.

lines.en: If the sun comes out, what will we do? I don’t want to stay inside.
lines.pt: Se o sol aparecer, o que faremos? Não quero ficar dentro de casa.

lines.en: If it’s sunny, we’ll walk along the canal and look at the old buildings.
lines.pt: Se estiver ensolarado, vamos andar ao longo do canal e olhar os prédios antigos.

lines.en: Lovely. If we get hungry, we’ll stop at a market and eat something local.
lines.pt: Lindo. Se ficarmos com fome, vamos parar num mercado e comer algo local.

lines.en: If there is a statue on the way, I’ll take a photo of you.
lines.pt: Se houver uma estátua no caminho, tiro uma foto sua.

lines.en: Thanks! If I find a nice souvenir, I’ll buy one for my mother.
lines.pt: Obrigado! Se eu achar uma lembrancinha bonita, compro uma para minha mãe.

lines.en: Perfect. If we plan well, we’ll have a wonderful holiday in Manchester.
lines.pt: Perfeito. Se planejarmos bem, teremos férias maravilhosas em Manchester.

items.wrong: If it will rain, we’ll visit the museum.
items.fix: If it rains, we’ll visit the museum.
items.why: After if, use the present simple, not will.

items.wrong: If I will find a souvenir, I’ll buy it.

items.why: Use the present simple after if.

items.wrong: If the sun comes out, we go to the canal tomorrow.

facts.label: Primeiro condicional
facts.sub: If it rains, we’ll visit the museum. We’ll walk if it is sunny. Nunca use will depois de if. A ordem das partes pode mudar.

facts.label: If + presente
facts.sub: Depois de if, use o presente simples, mesmo falando do futuro: If it rains, if we go early, if the sun comes out. Em português usamos o subjuntivo, mas em inglês o verbo fica simples.

facts.label: Will + verbo
facts.sub: Na parte do resultado, use will + verbo base: we’ll visit, I’ll buy, we’ll avoid. Contraia: I’ll, we’ll, you’ll. Evite will depois de if.

mini.en: Sure. If we go early, we’ll avoid {the queue|the crowd|the rain}. Museums are busy at ten.

mini.en: And if {the exhibition|the film|the tour} is boring, we’ll go to the gallery next door.

facts.label: Ordem

facts.label: Perguntas

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In the if part, we use the present simple.
We say “If it will rain, we’ll visit the museum”.
The result part uses will + verb.

The result part uses will + verb. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Rainy-day and sunny-day plans in Manchester · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey Thursday afternoon in Manchester. Joy and Leo sit at a table with a map and two cups of tea. Their holiday starts on Saturday. The weather forecast says it might rain. They decide to make two plans, one for rain and one for sun. Good plans start with the word if.

“Leo, if it rains on Saturday, we’ll visit the museum. Is that okay?” says Joy. “Sure. If we go early, we’ll avoid the queue. Museums are busy at ten.” says Leo. “Good idea. If we buy tickets online, we’ll save some time too.” says Joy.
